title: Elora Rocks hockey debt deferred, short-term rental licensing consultant hired
subtitle: Agri-food study deferred, provincial planning comments authorized, 2023 surplus moved to capital reserve, county blue box changes
overview: Council spent much of the evening on the Elora Rocks Hockey Club's request to forgive an interest-free loan owed to the Township. Rather than forgive or collect as is, Council deferred the matter and asked staff to bring back options for restructuring the debt by the June 10 meeting {{vote:m4}}.

Council awarded the short-term rental accommodation consulting contract to Maclaren Municipal Consulting Inc. at an upset limit of $74,900 excluding HST, funded from the general capital reserve {{vote:m5}}. The work will include public consultation ahead of a licensing by-law. Council also authorized planning staff to submit Township comments on the province's Spring 2024 Red Tape Reduction Package and draft Provincial Planning Statement {{vote:m6}}.

A delegation from the Wellington Federation of Agriculture presented its Agri-Food Systems Study. The motion to receive it was withdrawn, and consideration was deferred to the next meeting to allow public notice and consultation {{vote:m2}}. The consent agenda was approved, including a transfer of the 2023 operating surplus of $1,749,496 to the general capital reserve {{vote:m3}}. The County Council representative also briefed Council on the coming blue box changes.

decisions.item: Elora Rocks Hockey Club interest-free loan
decisions.detail: Council deferred a decision on the current agreement and directed staff to outline options for restructuring the debt, reporting back by the June 10 meeting.
Council awarded RFP #21-24 to Maclaren Municipal Consulting Inc. at an upset limit of $74,900 excluding HST, with a capital project funded from the general capital reserve.

decisions.item: Provincial red tape and planning statement comments
decisions.detail: Council authorized the Managing Director of Planning and Development to submit Township comments on the Ministry's Spring 2024 Red Tape Reduction Package and draft Provincial Planning Statement.
As part of the consent agenda, Council directed staff to transfer the 2023 year-end operating surplus of $1,749,496 to the general capital reserve.
Council deferred consideration of the Wellington County Agri-Food System Study to the next council meeting, after the original motion to receive it was withdrawn.

debate: Hockey club delegates said inherited debt, COVID and the games moved to Fergus during arena renovations strained finances. They asked for forgiveness and said they might step back if no solution was reached. They also said the club has no board, and that prior records were not available.

Councillors were divided on the loan. Some said the Township would likely lose the money either way and favoured a fresh start or refinancing. One councillor objected that forgiving it would treat the club differently from other ice users and set a precedent for other interest-free loan holders.

Staff said other groups must clear balances before booking again. They said the loan arrangement was brought to Council earlier, and a forgiveness would affect the 2024 operating budget. Council members asked about governance and community grants, and staff said grants cannot cover rent such as ice time.

On short-term rentals, councillors asked whether the licensing framework would cover issues such as parking and owner residency. Staff said public consultation with owners, neighbours and the hotel industry would shape the rules, and that a municipal accommodation tax is outside the scope.
On the agri-food study, a councillor asked that it be deferred so the public could see it on an agenda first. The mover agreed to withdraw the motion.
